summary: SCIM deprovision/upsert ordering race causes temporary admin role loss and 403s in private deployment
description: Customer reports that after performing SCIM-driven role changes via their IdP (NimbusData using an on-prem SCIM proxy) a subset of newly promoted admin users intermittently receive 403s when calling admin APIs for ~30-120s. The issue appears only in their private deployment and affects promotion workflows that happen alongside account deprovisioning (e.g., role moved from 'user'->'admin' while a scheduled deprovision job touches related group membership).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In customer IdP, schedule a SCIM job that: (a) PATCHes user to add 'admins' group membership (upsert style) and (b) shortly afterwards DELETEs a related placeholder group used by legacy workflows.
2) Observe event stream delivered to Redwood SCIM endpoint (customer uses on-prem SCIM proxy which batches events).
3) Immediately after the upsert, attempt to call an admin-only Redwood API as the promoted user.
4) Intermittently receive HTTP 403; retry after ~60-120s succeeds without additional actions.

comments: Customer (Elena from NimbusData): 'We see admins losing access right after our nightly deprovision/promotion task runs. Waiting a minute usually fixes it. This is blocking our cutover schedule.'
Support (Lena): 'Thanks — we've reproduced a similar pattern in our staging mirror when we replay your batch ordering. Sharing logs with infra team for RBAC cache analysis.'

SRE (Ravi): 'Preliminary: cache invalidation currently triggers on explicit DELETE/REMOVE events but not on PATCH upsert flows delivered in the same batch. If the DELETE clears a group referenced by the upsert, ordering can leave the cached roles stale until TTL expiry.'
Customer (Elena): 'We use an on-prem proxy that batches SCIM operations to reduce network chatter — can we change its ordering or disable batching?'
investigation_notes: Replayed customer's SCIM batch ordering in private staging; reproduced 403 window consistently when upsert and delete are delivered in single HTTP POST chunk.

SCIM handler processes events sequentially but RBAC invalidation logic treats 'group delete' as explicit cache invalidation only when the delete event explicitly references affected users; batched delete on group resource path currently doesn't emit per-user invalidation in our implementation.

Upsert (PATCH) path updates internal role mapping but does not force immediate cache refresh; relies on per-user invalidation which isn't emitted when group changes are deletions of placeholder groups.
Observed role_cache_ttl=60s in production for private clusters; TTL explains typical 30-120s window. Customer batch size averages 2-6 events in these jobs.

Config matrix: affected customers are using on-prem SCIM proxies that preserve IdP ordering but batch events in one HTTP request; hosted SCIM clients don't batch and so haven't reported this exact symptom.
temporary_workarounds: 1) Instruct customer to configure their SCIM proxy to send separate HTTP requests for upserts and deletes (introduce >200ms gap) so RBAC invalidation logic triggers correctly.
2) As support action, run manual role re-sync API for affected users: POST /admin/internal/roles/resync with user ids — this forces immediate invalidation and restores access.
3) Short-term cluster-side change: lower role_cache_ttl to 5s for the customer's private cluster (requires maintenance window). This reduces outage window but is disruptive for load.
4) Advise operators to avoid combining group DELETE of legacy placeholders in same batch as role-upsert promotions until permanent fix.
proposed_fix_plan: 1) Engineering to modify SCIM event processor to emit per-user invalidation for group DELETEs that reference membership lists or to synthesize 'membership-change' events when a batch contains both upsert and group-delete affecting the same users.
2) Add a fast-path: treat any PATCH upsert that modifies 'groups' field as a trigger to refresh the affected user's cache immediately (synchronously or best-effort async invalidation).
3) Add telemetry to measure 'batch-size vs cache-miss window' and run a 7-day canary in private staging before rolling to production clusters.
4) Update SCIM runbook and customer-facing guidance about batching behavior and recommended proxy settings for private deployments.
Estimated ETA: hotfix for cache invalidation in ~5 business days, staged rollout after canary in ~10 days.
next_steps: - Engineering (Ravi) to draft patch and open PR; include unit tests simulating batched payloads.
- Support (Lena) to schedule maintenance call with NimbusData to discuss temporary TTL change if they cannot change proxy batching quickly.
- Monitoring (SRE) to add an alert for sudden spikes in admin 403 rates post-SCIM job window.
- Document workaround in runbook page and link to customer-specific advisory.
